About Asian Disaster Preparedness Center

ADPC is an intergovernmental regional organization with a vision to reduce disaster and climate risk impacts on communities and countries in Asia and the Pacific by working with governments, development partners, international organizations, NGOs, civil society, private sector, media, and other key stakeholders. Established in 1986 as a technical capacity building center, ADPC has grown and diversified its expertise across social and physical sciences to support sustainable solutions for risk reduction across a broad range of specialist areas. With over 100 staff from 19 different nationalities and a wide range of professional expertise from atmospheric scientists to social scientists with experiences from all levels of engagement typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR) in an effective manner. ADPC is a competent regional resource center and has seven thematic departments: ADPC Academy, Risk Governance, Climate Resilience, Urban Resilience, Health Risk Management, Preparedness for Response and Recovery, Geospatial Information.

These are supported by Finance, Human Resources and Administration, and Strategic Planning departments. In addition to the departments, ADPC works on three cross-cutting themes: Gender and Diversity, Poverty and Livelihoods, and Regional and Transboundary Cooperation through permanent working committees. ADPC Strategy 2020 guides the organization in providing comprehensive risk reduction support to countries and communities in Asia and the Pacific. ADPC recognizes the importance of examining the linkages between disaster risk management, poverty reduction, gender equality, sustainability, rights-based approaches, climate change and regional cooperation. For details please refer to ADPC website at http://www.adpc.net/

Background

Disasters take a huge toll on the development agenda of SAR countries. Between 2000 and 2017, disasters in South Asia incurred estimated damages of US$ 149.27 billion. Public expenditure is under stress by the repeated need to reallocate capital budgets away from long term development planning and towards reconstruction activities in post-disaster environments. For example, since 2005, Pakistan has suffered losses on the order of US$ 16 billion due to natural disasters. In Bangladesh, 2007 Cyclone Sidr resulted in damages and losses of US$1.7 billion, or 2.6 per cent of GDP. To increase resilience and achieve climate commitments, there is a need for a transformational shift towards policies and institutions that enable climate-resilient investments. Investing in more resilient infrastructure is both profitable and urgent as disruptions are extremely costly for governments, households and private sector and large ongoing investments in infrastructure assets will have long-lasting repercussions as poor maintenance and natural disasters result in a vulnerable stock. With the financial support from the World Bank Group, ADPC will be implementing a five years’ project, titled “Climate Adaptation and Resilience Project for South Asia” (CARE).

The project aims to create an enabling environment for climate resilience policies and investments across South Asia. This objective will be achieved through enhanced regional cooperation and knowledge exchange for climate resilience and adaptation and mainstreaming of resilience and adaptation in national policies, plans and investments. Scaling up the climate resilient policy, planning, and financing is vital to satisfactorily implement all the required components of the project. It would involve review of national policies to support in development of climate resilient frameworks in planning and financing. Accordingly, a highly qualified and experienced Climate Policy and Planning Specialist will be required to support in reviewing national reports and frameworks. S/he will be selected on competitive basis following World Bank Procurement Regulations. The objectives of this consultancy service are to:

  • Country technical lead in reviewing, updating, and enhancing public policy and planning mechanisms related to climate resilience including institutional and related public expenditure.
  • Provide technical inputs in reviewing relevant country documents to highlight gaps in climate resilience with focus on public policy on climate resilience including planning mechanisms and public expenditure in Nepal.
  • Lead in facilitating cooperation between the Nepal Planning Commission, with the Ministry of Finance (MoF), Ministry of Forest and Environment (MOFE), the Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration (MOFAGA) and other critical public sector agencies in Nepal to identify gaps and develop an action plan for climate and disaster-risk informed investment.
  • Lead in the implementation of LAPA in a pilot province.

Statement of Intent

The Climate Policy and Planning Specialist will play an essential role in Nepal to ensure National expertise is available with a strong understanding of the processes key requirements, and stakeholders involved in developing development policy and plans to mainstream climate change. The Climate Policy and Planning Specialist will work closely with the Climate Policy and Planning Specialist in ADPC-Bangkok. The Climate Policy and Planning Specialist will be based in Kathmandu, Nepal. Note: It is not the intent of this Terms of Reference to cover every aspect of the position requirements, rather to highlight the most important areas of personal and joint responsibilities.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Climate Policy and Planning Specialist shall provide the following inputs:

Technical Review and Support

  • Assist and coordinate in organizing inception meeting/ consultations/ workshops in Nepal related to public policy and planning for climate resilience.
  • Co-lead (along with the Country Climate Finance Specialist) in review, of the Climate Public Expenditure and Institutional Review (CPEIR) with the Ministry of Forest and Environment (MoFE) and the Ministry of Finance (MoF), and the Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration (MOFAGA).
  • Provide support in reviewing documents on the country’s Climate Change Financing Framework (CCFF).
  • Provide inputs to develop a Nepal Action Plan for Climate and Disaster Risk Informed Investments supplemented by a National Appraisal and Approval Framework.

LAPA Development

  • Lead identifying, reviewing, and assessing the current status of country guidelines on local climate and disaster resilience developed for Nepal which complements the federalization process.
  • Lead in the co-development of provincial adaptation plan with local government, women’s group, CSOs, PWD groups, children’s group, and other stakeholders and integrate into sub-national development planning process and existing local DRR strategies.
  • Provide technical inputs into supporting the development of an implementation plan to roll out the climate change financing framework (CCFF) in the pilot province Tools and Guides Development.
  • Support the Climate Finance Specialist (ADPC country staff) in the development of National Guidelines for Nepal on Climate Finance and Planning by conducting preparatory review on climate policy and planning documents including country status on the implementation and develop an outline of Nepal Climate Policy, Planning and Finance National Guidelines.
  • Co-lead with the Climate Finance Specialist (ADPC country staff) in the establishment of a national technical working group (TWG) on Climate Finance and Planning composed of representatives from Ministry of Forest and Environment (MoFE) and the Ministry of Finance (MoF), and the Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration (MOFAGA), and other relevant government agencies and members of the Climate Change Network Nepal, including the development of a terms of reference and a draft roadmap to support the development of National Guidelines on Climate Policy, Planning and Finance.
  • Co-lead with the Climate Finance Specialist (ADPC country staff) in the development of a draft on the National Guidelines on Nepal Climate Policy, Planning and Finance supplemented with a roadmap for guideline process and implementation with the TWG including the process of sharing and submitting to the Nepal Planning Commission for review and approval.
  • Provide technical support in the analysis of the current status of the National Climate Change Budgeting and Planning in Nepal Performing other relevant tasks as assigned by the Project Director, Country Project Lead and Climate Policy and Planning Specialist (Regional).

Qualifications

  • A master’s degree of higher in Climate Change, International Development, Political Science, Public Administration or a relevant social science degree.
  • Minimum 7 years of experience in climate change and resilience and development policy analysis, and at least 5 years’ experience in policy and planning for resilient development.
  • Strong analytical skills and solid understanding of climate science, global frameworks, climate adaptation/resilience strategies, climate-informed policies and planning frameworks and sectoral interventions, global and national framework of climate services.
  • Knowledge of latest climate policies, frameworks such as Nepal’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), National Adaptation Plans (NAP), Local Adaptation Plan of Action Framework (LAPA), and other compliance and obligatory documents in the country relevant to climate adaptation and resilience.
  • Knowledge of national laws and government.
  • Proven research and analytical work.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills and capacity to work under pressure and short deadlines.
  • A professional relationship with the MoP and the MoFE is an advantage.
  • Cross cultural awareness and ability to work amongst a diverse group of staff, and partners.
  • Required computer proficiencies: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Microsoft Teams.
  • Experience in training, capacity building and facilitating high-level discussions.
  • Excellent English proficiency in oral and written communication, including a demonstrated track record in technical report writing and ability to communicate technical matters effectively to a general audience.

Reporting Relationships

The Climate Policy and Planning Specialist will report to Country Project Lead for the day to day activities and maintain close coordination with the ADPC’s Country Representative in Nepal. The technical oversight will be provided by the Climate Policy and Planning Specialist (Regional) at the Bangkok office through the PIU. The specialist will also coordinate with the other CARE project specialists at the regional and national level to carry out different activities under the project.

Selection Method

The consultant will be selected in accordance with ADPC’s recruitment process and in compliance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

TERMS OF REFERENCE

for the selection of a consulting/valuation company for the development of proposals for the Unified National Valuation Standards of the Republic of Uzbekistan based on international valuation standards.

 

1. Background information:

 According to the Decree of the president of the Republic of Uzbekistan
PD-4381 dated 01.07.2019, the Agency for state asset management, together with the Ministry of justice of the Republic of Uzbekistan, charged to take measures to approve unified national standards for the valuation of entities, regardless of the form of ownership, based on the principles of international valuation standards, taking into account the best foreign practices.

Unified national valuation standards of the Republic of Uzbekistan has been developed and registered by the Ministry of Justice and entered into force on September 5, 2020 (MJ registration No. 3229 dated June 4, 2020).

2. Goal:

Critically review and make changes, additions and adjustments to the existing Unified National Valuation Standards of the Republic of Uzbekistan (UNVS), based on the principles of international assessment standards, taking into account the best foreign practices, as well as national legislation.

Apply effective and transparent principles and methods for determining the value of assets.

Study and preparation of analytical materials on international best practices in the field of assessment according to international assessment standards (RICS, TEGOVA EVS, USPAP, IVS).

Revision of UNVS taking into account:

national legislation;

applying the principles of international valuation standards

at the national level (RICS, TEGOVA-EVS, USPAP, IVS);

developing a methodology for determining the value of assets;

practical application of UNVS in the Republic of Uzbekistan.

To achieve the objectives of this assignment, an international consulting/valuation company will be selected for the critical review and submission of specific proposals for making changes, additions and adjustments to the current version of UNVS.

Draft document on amendments to UNVS for registration with the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Uzbekistan

 

4. Principles of the work organization:

1. The project is implemented in compliance with the Program of the Project and plans of works, timely and within the budget;

2. Effectively implemented and well-managed project in accordance with the procedures of the World Bank and the legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan;

3. Efficient interaction with all participants in the project (appraisal organizations, public organizations in the field of appraisal activities, Agency for state assets management and etc.);

4. To perform this ToR, the international Consulting/valuation company interacts with the Agency for state assets management in relation to all technical and coordination aspects.

5. Performance indicators of the international consulting/valuation company.

The effectiveness of the international consulting/valuation company’s work will be assessed according to the following indicators:

timeliness of preparation of plans / reports within the framework of this TOR and in accordance with clause 3 "Scope of work" of this TOR;

completeness of materials on international best practices in the field of valuation according to international valuation standards in the light of the priority areas of economic reforms carried out in the Republic of Uzbekistan;

detailed analysis of differences and discrepancies in assessment methods

according to international valuation standards and UNVS, with details for each standard;

completeness of the package of documents for the introduction and approval by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Uzbekistan of amendments and additions to the existing UNVS or the adoption of the UNVS in a new edition, including indicating the methodology (s) for determining the value of assets.

6. Expected result

The expected long-term results of the development of proposals and, if necessary, revision of UNVS include the following:

determining the value of assets through the use of effective and transparent approaches and assessment methods;

improving the quality and practice of assessment in all sectors of the economy;

use of progressive methods and tools of the assessment process;

raising the qualifications and professional level of appraisers through familiarization with international practice and the application of international valuation standards;

Providing the Report on suggestions and comments on the necessary adjustments to the UNSO of the Republic of Uzbekistan based on the studied material.

7. Qualification Requirements to the Consultant

An international consulting / valuation company is required (specialists from an international consulting / appraisal company must have strong communication skills in English and Russian).

Work experience requirements.

- Practical experience in the valuation of various assets (valuation of business, commercial real estate, movable property) for a period of at least 10 years, at the international level and in certain regions: the countries of Europe, the CIS and Central Asia. Work experience in Uzbekistan is an advantage.

- Practical experience in performance of certain activities requested in the ToR;

Qualifications requirements

- The head of an international consulting / valuation company must be a professional appraiser with both international and regional work experience. Must have at least one of the international qualifications (CFA, RICS, ASA, TEGoVA). Knowledge of UNVS and the legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan will be an advantage;

- Specialists of an international consulting / valuation company should have relevant experience in working groups for the development of standards and / or legislative regulations for valuation activities. Experience must be confirmed by the presence of at least 1 (one) letter of recommendation.

8. Duration of the Contract:

The duration of the contract is 6 months from the date of signing. The contract may be extended if independent circumstances (e.g. the situation with COVID-19) have a negative impact on the terms of the contract.

 

9. Resources, provided by the (State agencies):

7.1. Establishment of a Working Group out of specialists of the (state agencies) for interaction with the international consulting/valuation company during implementation of this ToR;

7.2. Ensuring the international consulting/valuation company’s communication and interaction with the state agencies during the assessment of the state of affairs, as well as the implementation of this project;

10. Terms of financing services:

The sources of financing will be funds from World Bank Group through the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) under the Ministry of Finance.

At the same time, the international consulting/valuation company is accountable and reports to the Agency in accordance with the Scope of Work, presenting a report and acts of work performed.

The relationship between the international consulting/valuation company and the Agency with the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) under the Ministry of Finance is carried out in accordance with the established procedure through the Agency. At the same time, the international consulting/valuation company must:

1. Timely provide the developed materials specified in paragraph 3 "Scope of work" of this TOR;

2. Provide summary reports on the progress of the project, within two weeks after the reporting period;

3. Develop a final project report in a format acceptable to the World Bank and ASAM within one month after the completion of the project.

All plans / reports should be written in Russian and English and sent by e-mail to the World Bank and ASAM.

Ministry of Rural Development

Cambodia Agricultural Sector Diversification Project

 (CASDP)  IDA Credit No. 6366 KH

Request for Expressions of Interest (REOI)

NATIONAL FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT ASSISTANT CONSULTANT

  1. General Background

The Royal Government of Cambodia has received a Credit of US$91.67 million from International Development Association (IDA) for the project costs including and the Government’s support in form of counterpart financing amounts to US$10.00 million, including the equivalent of US$4million in-kind contributions, the use of office space, staff costs and utility expenses, and US$6 million contributing to the component 2 of public infrastructure support to the total costs of US$29.33 million would be joint financing with counterpart funding with pro-rata basis.

  1. The objective of the Assignment

The objective of the National Financial Management Assistant Consultant is to assist Chief/Finance Officers at CASDP-MRD and working with other consultants to follow the Term of Reference and action plan to record in a timely, efficient, and transparent manner in line with the Project Operational Manual (POM), Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB), Procurement Plan (PP) and Progress Report as the deadline for submission to Government and Bank in supporting financial management supports to the project’s FM team to ensure the successful timely implementation and completion of the finance-related activities. It is expected that the selected consultant will at all times observe the highest standard of professional ethics and integrity, and promote a results-oriented approach in the area of his/her responsibility and accountability.

  1. Term of References and Scope of Work:
  2. Support the project in implementing financial controls and procedures in the Project Operations Manual;
  3. Help to post financial transactions into the accounting software (Sage 50) and ensure correct classification of the financial transactions;
  4. Maintain contract registers for contracts of goods, works, and services, and ensure accuracy of entries and updated records at all times;
  5. Maintain registers for cash advances and fixed assets procured from the project;
  6. Assist the FM team of CASDP-MRD in preparing required supporting documents for disbursement purposes such as the statement of expenditures, reconciliation of the designated account (bank account), etc. for the replenishment of the Designated Account and documentation of expenditure;
  7. Assist the FM team in monitoring implementation of the budget by tracking each budget request to the approved activity budget;
  8. Assist the FM team in doing accounts reconciliation;
  9. Follow up late liquidation of cash advances by monitoring due dates of liquidation and

providing reminders to relevant departments and staff;

  1. Assist the FM team in reviewing Petty Cash replenishments;
  1. Assist the FM team in the preparation of relevant financial reports for submission to the Project Management, the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), and WB;
  2. Assist in the FM team in collaboration with the EA-FM and IAs- FM, internal

auditor, external auditor, and mission team by providing information as requested;

  1. Help the project in timely submission of monthly tax declaration;
  1. Perform other tasks as may be requested by the Project Manager.
  1. Qualification and Experience Requirements

To be qualified for the position the candidates must meet the minimum required qualifications as follows:

  1. a Bachelor Degree in Accounting or Finance or a related field;
  2. 5 years of working experiences in accounting and financial management systems of the project or non-profit organization or company;
  3. Preferably, at least 3-year experience in implementing financial management procedures of projects financed by DPs, and the Government’s standard operating procedures (SOP) in the Financial Management Manual (FMM) for all externally financed projects/programs in Cambodia;
  4. Familiar with accounting software operation; Sage 50 (Peachtree) is preferred;
  5. Fluency in written and spoken English and Khmer, as a most Khmer Unicode;
  6. Computer literate with a thorough knowledge of the standard computer programs such as MS-Word, MS-Excel, Ms-PowerPoint, Email, and Internet, etc.

The Ministry of Rural Development invites expressions of interest from qualified and experienced candidates to undertake the above mentioned services which are further detailed in the Terms of Reference for the assignments. The selection process will be carried out in accordance with provisions set forth in the Government Procurement Manual for Externally Financed Projects/Programs in Cambodia and Approved Selection Method for Individual Consultants-Section VII. “Approved Selection Methods: Consulting Services of the World Bank Procurement

Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated July 2016, revised November 2017 and August 2018”.

V.         How and where to apply. Interested candidates may obtain further information on the detailed Terms of Reference (in English) for the assignment from the address giving below:

CASDP-MRD office address:  Cambodia Agricultural Sector Diversification Project. Ground floor building of Ministry of Rural Development. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Re-advertisement for additional candidates

 (CONSULTING SERVICES FIRMS SELECTION)

 

GOVERNMENT OF VIET NAM

MEKONG DELTA WATER RESOURCES MANAGEMENT FOR RUAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECT

Credit No: 4951-VN

Assignment Title: Preparation of provincial watermanagement & investment plans

Reference No (as per procurement plan): CPMU-GT02

The Government of Viet nam has received a creditfrom the International Development Association (IDA), toward the costof theMekong delta water resources management for rural development project,and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services forNationalConsultant Firm for Updating Provincial Water Management and Investment Plans.

The consulting services ("the Services") includethe main contents as follows:

  • Assignment objectives of  Consultant services are  as follows: (1) Preparing an updated watermanagement and investment plan, for each province located in the western partof the Mekong Delta in accordance with the master plans for water resources inthe Mekong Delta and other relevant master plans, taking into accounttheimpacts of the development in the upstream Mekong River Basin and climatechange-sea level rise. Explore non-structural measures and especiallyinstitutional arrangements for better and sustainable operation; (2) Planningand upgrading water resources infrastructure and systems in the western part ofthe Mekong Delta including reforming institutional arrangement and operationand maintenance systems to solve issues on flooding, salinity intrusion,sedimentation, erosion, navigation, water supply, drainage, and acidification;(3) Identifying a portfolio of water resources systems in each province toprovide basis for preparation of 5-year plans, annual plans, programsandprojects in the provinces of the study area; and (4) Recommend institutionalarrangements for operation and management of water management/ irrigationstructures .

  • Scopeof the consulting services comprises as follows: The Consultant will work closelywith DWRs, CPMU, and the target provinces to ensure achievement of theobjectives of this technical assistance, and the outcomes should comply withthe following aspects:

  1. The provincial water management and investment plansmust be based on information, data and materials with high reliability.

  2. The updating has to conform with the basic tasks ofregional plans in terms of  targets ofkey industries, key projects, the flagship product, ensuring uniformity of scale,progress, phasing, priority and capabilities of the resources for development planning in order topropose solutions for plan implementation, measures of plan management in thewestern Mekong Delta.

  3. The updating has to conform with the previous nationaland international studies related to the study area, the Mekong Deltaand theMekong River Basin; especially the Master Plan for Socio-economic Developmentin the Mekong Delta until 2020, and the Master Plan for Water ResourcesDevelopment in the Mekong Delta under the Context of the Climate Change-SeaLevel Rise specified in the Decision No.1397/QD-TTg.

  4. The updating has to use the results of assessments ofthe impacts of climate change-sea level rise based on updated information overthe world and Vietnam's coastal area to determine planning options.

Georgia

Consulting Services

Grant No. TF014363

Expressions of interest

 

Georgia has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (World Bank) towards the cost of the Project Capacity Building for Georgia's National Examination Center (NAEC) from the World Bank's Institutional Development Fund (IDF) Grant No.TF014363. The purpose ofthe Project is to strengthen the effectiveness of the Georgia's general education system through (i) building capacity in the areas of teacher and school principal evaluation, and (ii) improving access to information on the existing teacher policies.  More specifically, the project will support: (a) capacity building of the core staff ofNAEC; (b) introduction of new evaluation methods in the existing teacher certification system; (c) design of a credible and comprehensive system for the selection and evaluation of principals of general education schools; and (d) conducting the World Bank's benchmarking instrument - Systems Approach for Better Education Results (SABER) on teacher policies.

 

NAEC intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services to develop concept paper on principals' evaluation and lead task force/stakeholders workshop. Main duties and responsibilities of theconsultant will be:

 

1)       Utilize a situation analysis prepared by the administrative international consultant in order to  develop a concept paper on a system for principals certification, selection and performance assessment;

2)       Advise and provide recommendations for development of a national model for principal selection, evaluation and professional development;

3)       Suggest a vision (immediate, mid- and long term perspective) and an action plan to the Ministry of Education for development of a national School Principals' selection and performance-based evaluation model and other relevant regulations as per the needs identified;

4)       Assist NAEC staff in practical development of assessment tools for school principals;

5)       Conduct trainings/workshops for a NAEC task force on principles and strategies of the evaluation of school principals;

6)       Support  NAEC in planning and organizing relevant  study tours in order to strengthen task force capacity,

7)       Consult and advise the NAEC task force throughout conducting consultations and focus group meetings with stakeholdersand beneficiaries;

8)       Cooperate extensively with the selected International consultants recruited by NAEC within the capacity building project , in particular, the administrative consultant and teacher certification and evaluation consultant, for designing and  strengthening school principals' selection and evaluation system;

NAEC nowinvites eligible individual consultant(s) to indicate their interest in providing the services mentioned above.

Interested candidates meeting requirements below shall send motivation letter and CV describing their similar experience and qualification.

 

General Requirements:

         Doctoral (PHD) or other equivalent degree from an internationally recognized university in education or any other relevant field or equivalent mix of education and experience;

         Theoretical knowledge of public sector policy formulation,institutional development and advocacy with multiple stakeholders;

         Knowledge of international education and development;

         Demonstrated high level written and verbal communication skills in English.

         Availability for the assignment period (Mar Dec, 2014) and conducting at least three visits of duration 7 calendar days or more for each visit;

         Knowledge of Georgia country context and education reform initiatives will be an asset.

Relevant Experience:

 

         Minimum of ten (10) years professional experience in education, including knowledge and experience inthe certification of principals;

         A minimum of five (5) years international experience on principals licensure and evaluation projects;

         Ppractical experience in publicsector policy formulation, specifically, of General Education policy, experience of institutional development and advocacy with multiple stakeholders;

         Experience of working on similar projects for principals' performance appraisal and certification systems.

'

No.D'd.VE.ll-111/37/13                                                                                              Dt. 21.02.2014

Request for Expression of Interest (REol) For Consultancy services for Senior Engineer in Berhampur Municipal Corporation,Berhampur for World Bank Funded Project.


The BeMC, Berhampur under Odisha Disaster Recovery Project (ODRP) funded by the World Bank requires consultancy services for Senior Engineer in Berhampur MunicipalCorporation,Berhampur.


The detailed terms and conditions for submission of REol are indicated in Draft Terms of Reference and REol that shall be available on our web site

www.berhampur.gov.in

with effect from 22-02-2014


Interest consultants are required to submit their REol with the required details and supporting documents latest by 10-03-2014 up to 4.00 PM at the addressed mentioned in REol.

Please visit the website www.berhampur.gov.in for any clarification.

Municipal Commissionerer

Berhampur Municipal corporation



1. Background of project


1.1 General

DRAFT TERMS OF REFERENCE

The Government of India has applied for financing from the World Bank towards cost of the Odisha Disaster Recovery Project (ODRP), and Berhampur municipal Corporation intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for

"Project Management, Supervision and Quality control Consultancy in the Project Implementation Unit (PIU)" based in Berhamapur and in Project Management Unit (PMU) based in Bhubaneswar. Component 2: Community Infrastructure Investments in Berhampur of the ODRP will be implemented by the BeMC under the aegis of the Housing and Urban Development Department of Government of Odisha.

Berhampur city is the fourth most populous urban area in the stateof Orissa. It is mainly a trading centre for Southern Orissa having its influence over eight districts. It is the oldest city of Ganjam District. The

city of Berhampur isgoverned by the Berhampur Municipal Corporation (BeMC). BeMC's jurisdiction covers an area of about 37 sq.km. and has a population of over 378,000.

Berhampur slums

: There are 254 slum settlementsaccommodating 28,270 households and a population of 126,541. Slum population is thus 33.41 % of the total population. Many of them are located around the

47 water bodies in the city, mainly in the form of tanks and alongthe natural or built drains. In the absence of sewerage system in thecity, these water courses also carry septic tank effluents or the untreated human waste. The slums are therefore vulnerable to both flood and health hazards. Shelters in

slums vary in construction from reeds and mud walls with thatched roofs to brick walls with AC or GI

sheets as roof. The latter are vulnerable to strong winds and the former to heavy rains. Government of

Odisha intends to improve the shelters under Government of India programs, including Rajiv Awas Yojna

(RAY).


The Berhampur Municipal Corporation proposes to undertake various urban infrastructure projects, in particular the slum improvement works with a view to provide better facilities to the people living in slum areas. The works spread over entire Municipal Corporation area.


1.2 It is proposed to engage qualified consultants with proven relevant experience of providing project management support for the projects of similar nature and size, including for the supervision and quality control of proposed/ ongoing works. The proposed works involve construction / up gradation / renewal of various urban infrastructure investments including some city level infrastructure.


1.3 Component 2 of ODRP


1.

Sub-component 2.1: Upgrading of slums - US$15 million. For infrastructure to improve the living conditions of households in slums in the city of Berhampur. Theseimprovements include streets, access to improved water and sanitation, drainage, septic management, and street lighting. The level of service to be provided will be determined by the available trunk infrastructure, the physical conditions, size of the settlements, and the available resources. The project will be carried out in about 80 settlementscovering about 30,000 population.

2.

Sub-component 2.2: Public service infrastructure - US$11.7 million. For priority infrastructure at

the city level to improve service delivery and living conditions. The BeMC has carried out an assessment of damage and needs after Cyclone Phailin from which an investment plan is being prepared. Investments include priority roads and trunk water supply infrastructure among others.

3.

Subcomponent 2.3: Community participation - US$1.7 million. This component will help facilitate community participation, ensuring a participatory approach in the planning ofsettlement level

infrastructure.

4.

Sub-Component 2.4: Technical Assistance - US$1.7 million. For providing support to the BeMC

towards preparation of improved city-wide sectoral master plans and priority Detailed Project Reports

(DPRs). These will include drainage, sewerage, street lighting andother relevant areas identified.


2. Objective of the Assignment

The main objective of the assignment is to provide support to BeMCand assist in preparation of DPRs for

Component 2 under ODRP.


Key tasks:

Based on the identified slums,and other city level infrastructure work such as arterial roads, water supply network collect all information necessary for planning and designing of the infrastructure works, that includes obtaining layout/alignment maps, levels and bringing in missing information.

Prepare detailed designs, cost estimates, bidding documents, packaging information and

procurement plan etc. and revise based on review by the PIU/PMU/World Bank.

Assist the PIU in obtaining approvals, bidding, evaluation and contract award.

Attend meetings and support in preparing necessary information, notes etc.

Assist in the preparation of terms of reference, request for proposals and evaluation of tender documents submitted by bidding firms for engineering related assignments.

Work and coordinate with otherexperts as required.

3. Duration:

The contract is for 6 months with provision for further extension.

4. Key Qualifications:

Civil Engineer with post graduation in public health engineering with minimum of 15 years of relevant experience.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

Selection of consultant for advisory support on chlorination in water treatment

 

COUNTRY:  Kyrgyz Republic

NAME OF PROJECT:  "Second Rural Water Supply Project"

Grant#H462-KG, Credit#4560-KG

 

Assignment Title: Advisory support on chlorination in water treatment

 

Reference No.: IDA-RWSSP-IC-2013-7

 

The Kyrgyz Republic's Community Development and Investment Agency (ARIS) has been established in support of sustainable poverty alleviation in Kyrgyz Republic by assisting local self-governments in addressing local social and economic issues.

 

This goal is being achieved through implementation, as an Implementing Agency, of a number of Public Investment Program projects (Projects) financed through funds provided to the Kyrgyz Republic by international donors.

 

One of the main projects implemented by ARIS is the World Bank-financed Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Project-2 (RWSSP-2). Theproject is aimed to assist the Kyrgyz Republic to (i) improve access to potable water for participating communities; (ii) promote hygiene, sanitation and water-related practices at individual, family and institutional level in rural areas; and (iii) strengthen institutional framework and capacities to sustain continued RWSS sector development. 

 

RWSSP-2 is actively dealing with institutional development of water supply and sanitation sector. Ensuring high standards of drinking water quality is a critical feature of the strategy on water supply in the Kyrgyz Republic. Virtually all public supplies are chlorinated - about 98 percent of North American and European water treatment systems use chlorine.  Any raw water supply source from lakes or rivers will contain organisms. Chlorine is used to remove micro-organisms from water.  Water supplied via pipelines may spend days moving through the system before it gets to the consumer.  Chlorine added to the water will reduce the chance of micro-organisms multiplying in the pipes or storage tanks.  The art of the water treatment plant operators is to add enough chlorine to fix the risk of micro-organisms, but not to add too much so that consumers complain about the smell and taste of the chemical.  Disinfection by chlorine has been standard practice for nearlya hundred years.  The use of chlorine as a disinfectant has saved hundreds of thousands of lives by making drinking water safe. 

 

The current public debate about chlorination concerns the direct health impact from ingesting chlorine and the by-products that may be formed in chlorinated drinking water[1]. This debate has received significant traction in the Kyrgyz Republic and it is important that an international expert is contracted to help bring some perspective and clarity in understanding of this debate.  In doing so the expert will provide an opportunity to provide international experience and knowledge, and assist setting a course for a robust disinfection strategy for water treatment.

 

The assignment has two objectives:

1)      Assessment of the current situation and analysis of the applicability of new, potentially automated technologies that could be used to simplify and streamline chlorination even for small rural water schemes. 

2)      Preparationof guidelines and providing training of trainers on chlorination use in water treatments.

 

The Community Development and Investment Agency (ARIS) as an Implementing Agency of the Project,  now invites  qualified individuals  ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information (CV) demonstrating thatthey have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

Qualification requirements:

         At least 10 years of experience in water treatment and in particular disinfection techniques

         International experience of water treatment and the circumstances/challenges facing different countries

         Good writing skills, especially in the preparation of Guideline documents

         Experience in developing and conducting training

         Fluency in English required, fluency in Russian is desirable.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank'sGuidelines: Selection and Employmentof Consultants by World Bank Borrowers  published in May 2004, Revised October 2006 and May 2010 ("Consultant Guidelines"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. 

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with  the  Individual selection  (IC) method.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 9:00 to 18:00 hours, Mondaythrough Friday.

 

CV's with the cover letter  must be delivered in a written form to the address below  by  November  8,2013.

 

Community Development and Investment Agency (ARIS)

Attn: Mrs.Damira Temirbaeva,ARIS Procurement specialist

102, Bokonbaeva Str.

720040, Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic

Tel: + 996 (312) 62-07-52, 30-18-05 

Fax: +996 (312)62-47-48

E-mail: amambetkulova@aris.kg;dtemirbaeva@aris.kg;

Web site: aris.kg


[1] There are reports that indicate that free chlorine causes fats to form cholesterol deposits that may clog arteries. Chlorine can alsodestroy beneficial vitamin E.  Vitamin E prevents the formation of free radicals (destructive molecules that promote tissue breakdown and tumour formation). One class of chemical compounds formed as disinfection by-products is called tri-halomethanes.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

KAZAKHSTAN

Name of the assignment:  

 

Contract No. KHSTTIRP-F/CS-02, Consulting services for harmonization of Standards for Food Safety indexes including MRLs of Nitrates, Radionuclides, Antibiotics and Veterinary Drugs in Food stipulated by Technical Regulations of Customs Union to meet international requirements.

 

The Republic of Kazakhstan has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Health Sector Technology Transfer and Institutional Reform Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consultant services under Contract Ref: KHSTTIRP-F/CS-02 for harmonization of Standards for Food Safety indexes including MRLsof Nitrates, Radionuclides, Antibiotics and Veterinary Drugs in Food stipulated by Technical Regulations of Customs Union to meet international requirements.

 

The Objective of this assignmentis the technical and methodological assistance to the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Kazakhstan in harmonization of standards of Food Safety indexes including MRL of nitrates, radionuclides, antibiotics and veterinary drugs in food stipulated by technical regulations of Customs Union  to meet international requirements.

 

 

Expected duration of the assignment:

Period of consultation services is 18 months.

 

 

Scope of Services: it is expected that the consulting company (Consultant) will provide technical and methodological support to the Ministry of Health in the following general issues:

Harmonization of standards of Food Safety indexes including MRLs of nitrates, radionuclides, antibiotics and veterinary drugs in food stipulated by technical regulations of Customs Union  to meet international requirements.

 

      i.          to  formulate list of standards containing rules and testing methods and measurements including sampling procedures required for application and execution of technical regulation available in member-statesof Customs Union, EC to meet Codex Alimentarius requirement that are absent in Kazakhstan;

    ii.          to prepare recommendations and proposals to enter for review by Euroasian Economic Commission related to sanitary and epidemiological welfare (Food Safety) given national interests of Kazakhstan including taken decisions on Customs Union standardsbeing introduced into force;

  iii.          jointly with CSSES MOH RK to enter developed standards to CTRM MINT RK  registration;

  iv.          making the list of standards and Sanitary rules of MRL of nitrates, radionuclides, antibiotics and veterinary drugs in food;

    v.          to assure list of standards containingrules and testing methods and measurements including sampling procedures required for application and execution of technical regulation available in member-states of Customs Union, EC to meet Codex Alimentarius requirement that are absent in Kazakhstan;

  vi.          comparative analysis of current hygienic standards of  MRL of nitrates, radionuclides, antibiotics and veterinary drugs in food of animal and plant origin in Kazakhstan and EC;

vii.          submission of international risk assessment for set MRL of nitrates, radionuclides,  antibiotics and veterinary drugs and feeds for the following group of food products:

- beef, mutton, poultry, horse meet, pork;

- cow milk;

- potato, carrot, onion, purple, apples, strawberries.

 

 

Expected outcomes:

It is expected that the implementation of assignment will result in harmonization of MRL for nitrates, radionuclides, antibiotics and veterinary drugs in food is done in compliance with the international requirements.

 

 

Qualification requirements:

 

1.    Detailed profile of international experts is defined by the scope of works under this TORs and includes proven experience in the following areas:

a)      Development of draft laws and regulatory documents on food safety in accordance with Codex Alimentarius requirements;

b)      Familiarity with WTO regulatory documents and standards on sanitary and phyto-sanitary measures;

c)                  Provisions of SPS;

d)                 Development and implementation of integrated national food safety system;

e)                  Technological processes and organization of food safety control;

f)                   Organization of food safety laboratory control, expertise in laboratory equipment and services, and accreditation of food safety laboratory service;

g)                  Development and implementation of monitoring system for food products;

h)                  Development and implementation of capacity building programs in food control;

i)        Development and implementation of information, education and communications campaigns in food safety.

TheGovernment of Liberia (GoL) through the Civil Service Agency (CSA) has received financing from the World Bank to support the strengthening of governance and public administration through the Public Sector Modernization Project (PSMP).  The Civil Service Agency intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring a highly organized and energized Procurement Specialist who will carry on with the procurement function under the project and continue the capacity building of the procurement officers in the participating ministries and agencies.

 

The objectives of the assignment

The objective of the assignment of the Procurement Specialist is in two-fold:

         Supplement the capacity of the CSA to manage the procurement activities under the project hereafter called the "Client", including the planning and implementation and supervision of all procurement operations under the project; and

 

         Continue with the development of procurement capacity to facilitate activation of procurement activities in participating ministries and agencies and build their capacity to gradually take over the procurement function at the end of the consultancy period.

 

The duration of the assignment:

The timescale of the assignment is for an initial period of twelve (12) staff months (one year) and may be renewed subject to satisfactory performance. The duty station shall be Civil Service Agency Monrovia, Liberia. However, a portion of this assignment could be undertaken away from Monrovia

The Civil Service Agency now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services by submitting their detailed information (CV'sdescribing similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, etc).  Selection will be based on qualifications and experience stipulated below.

 

Consulting firms are allowed to propose individuals for this assignment. However, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shallbe used in the selection process, and corporate experience shall not be taken into account and the contract would be signed with the proposed individual.

 

Required Minimum Qualifications:

  • Masters degree in relevant discipline e.g. Procurement, Business, Law, Public Administration, Engineering etc with a minimum of 5 years experience in procurement and contract management in the public sector, or first degree in relevant discipline with minimum 10 years experience in procurement and contract management in the public sector;;
  • Minimum of 5 years' working experience in handling andmanaging international competitive procurement in World Bank funded or administered projects is a must;
  • Knowledge of ProjectManagement, appropriate involvement and/or experience in similar projects in developing countries.
  • Must have good knowledge of procurement policies and procedures of multilateral financial institutions (e.g.the World Bank) and development co-operation agencies; as well as good knowledge of the institutional, technical, and commercial aspects ofprocurement;
  • Experience / Skills to train / mentor procurement staff is a requirement
  • Experience of similar assignments in the Region is highly preferred.
  • Fluency in spoken English and ability to write lucid reports and documents in English is required.
  • Strong organization skills and ability to work in a team-oriented, culturally diverse environment.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, sound judgment, communication skills, training experience,ability to identify and resolve policy and operational constraints.
  • Must be able to demonstrate computer skills and knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite
  • Ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously, set priorities, and work independently, or under minimum supervision.

 

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants by World Bank Borrowers (January 2011). ("Consultant Guidelines), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the procedures set out in Section V of the World Bank's Guidelines: Selectionand Employment of Consultants under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants by World Bank Borrowers" dated January 2011.

Interested Consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours from 09:00 and 17:00hours, Mondays to Fridays.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form clearly marked:  "Ref: Procurement Specialist of the PSMP", at the address below in person or by mail or by email) on or before Monday, July  8, 2014 at 16:00hours.

The Projector Coordinator

Public Sector Modernization Project

Civil Service Agency

63 Carey Street, Monrovia, Liberia

Email: publicsectormodernizationcsa@gmail.com

Attention: The Project Coordinator-PSMP

The Russian Federation has received financing fromthe World Bank toward the cost of the Second State Statistical SystemDevelopment Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for developing methodology for recording intellectual property products in the national accounts.

The consulting services ("the Services") include the development of methodological guidelines for recording intellectual property products in national accounts in accordance with 2008 SNA concept.

To fulfill the assignment, the Consultant should:

-  review international recommendations, study and summarize practices of national statistical offices in this area;

-  assess applicability of the international practices of recording intellectual property products in national accounts under the conditions of Russia;

-  review available statistical data, statistical forms and methods for collecting data needed for recording intellectual property products in thenational accounts;

-  develop methodological approaches to recording specific groups of intellectual property products in the national accounts in accordance with 2008 SNA concepts and with a consideration for the peculiarities of Russian statistical system;

-  develop methodological recommendations for implementing into the nationalaccounts of the Russian Federation methods of recording intellectual property products in accordance with the 2008 SNA standards.

An estimated duration of the assignment is 14 months.

 

 The Bureau of Economic Analysis Foundation appointed as Project Implementation Unit of the Second State Statistical System Development Project now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria are:

The Consultant shall be an independent company with sufficient experience in carrying out similar work and with awareness of the Russian economy, methodology and practices of national accounting, system of enterprise, business, and tax accounting. This company shall have successful experience and organizational resources to fulfill this assignment within the indicated time frame. The Consultant shall be specialized inrendering consulting services, including those on developing statistical indicators, shall have experience in conducting research and in implementing similar projects in the Russian Federation and/or other countries.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 and 1.11 of the World Bank's Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers, May 2004, revised October 2006 and May 2010  ("Consultant Guidelines"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest and eligibility.

 

Consultants may submit their Expressions of Interest as an individual firm or in association in the form of a joint venture or subconsultancy. All the members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment. However, the experience of sub-consultant will not be considered while short-listing.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the QCBS (Quality- and Cost-Based Selection) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines.

Further information can beobtained at the address below during office hours from 11:00 to 17:00 hours.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by fax, or by e-mail) by June 16, 2014.
